# SOC 2 Control Matrix

The spreadsheet that lists every control Quaylane asserts for SOC 2, who owns it, how often it runs and where its evidence lives. First complete version on 2026-03-02; frozen for the Type II window on 2026-09-01. It is the single document an auditor, an investor or a new engineer should read first to understand what we have promised.

## Summary

58 controls mapped to the Security, Availability and Confidentiality [[trust-services-criteria]]. Each row has an ID, a plain description, owner, frequency, evidence type and the folder in the [[soc2-evidence-folder]] where evidence lands. 31 controls are owned by engineering (me, [[kwabena-asare]], [[teodora-vasilescu]]), 14 by [[colette-fairbanks]] (people and vendors), 9 by [[renata-castellano]] (governance, risk assessment, board oversight) and 4 by customer success ([[imani-brooks]]).

## Why It Matters

The matrix decides what we must do every week to keep the Type II clean. Three rows matter most because they are recurring, easy to skip, and the ones auditors sample hardest:

- **CM-01 Change management.** Every change to `main` in the four production repositories has one recorded approval, enforced by branch protection; emergency changes follow [[ship-an-emergency-change]] and are logged. Evidence: GitHub pull request records and the [[github-organization-audit-log]]. This row is why the rule from [[engineering-meeting-2026-04-08]] exists.
- **AC-04 Quarterly access review.** Every quarter the owner of each system confirms who has access and removes anyone who should not. Evidence: the signed review sheet per quarter. This row produced Type I exception 1 ([[soc2-type-1-report]]); procedure in [[run-the-quarterly-access-review]].
- **HR-07 Offboarding.** Access removed within one business day of the last day; company laptop returned and wiped, with a wipe record. This row produced Type I exception 2.

## Key Details

- Column set: `id`, `criteria` (e.g. CC6.1), `control`, `owner`, `frequency` (continuous, per event, monthly, quarterly, annual), `evidence`, `evidence_path`, `tested_type1`, `type2_samples`.
- Readiness review on 2026-04-20 marked 11 rows as gaps; 9 were closed before the as-of date of 2026-07-31 ([[soc2-readiness-review-2026-04-20]]).
- Other engineering rows: production access via SSO with MFA (AC-01), least-privilege IAM roles reviewed annually (AC-06, see [[principle-of-least-privilege]]), encrypted databases and backups (DP-02), vulnerability scanning on dependencies (VM-01), annual penetration test (VM-03), incident response (IR-01, which points to [[run-an-incident]]), backup restore test twice a year (AV-03).
- The superseded first checklist is [[soc2-readiness-checklist-2026-02]].

## Caveats

The matrix records what we assert, not what an auditor has tested. The Type I tested design and implementation as of one day; operating effectiveness is only tested in the Type II. Do not edit rows during the window without agreeing it with [[patrice-ndour]].

## Source Location

Shared drive, `Security/SOC2/control-matrix.xlsx`, owner Nikolas Arneberg, edit rights Nikolas and Colette only. Version history in the drive.
